subject: Acme pilot - concurrency & rate limits follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cheng <alan.cheng@acme.io>, Samantha Pierce <samantha@acme.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme pilot - post-call recap and next steps (concurrency / streaming)

Hi Alan & Samantha,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through Acme's in-app assistant use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance requirements and how Redwood can support them for the pilot: 

Summary of what I heard:
- UX requirement: streaming token-by-token responses for the assistant UI with visible latency < 200ms for first byte on most queries.
- Typical prompt/response size: ~250 tokens avg, with occasional long-form responses up to ~1,000 tokens.
- Expected peak active users: ~12k during business hours; rough concurrency estimate you mentioned is 600-800 parallel in-flight requests.
- Connection model: you prefer HTTP/2 connection reuse and client-side pooling (keep-alive) to reduce handshake overhead.

What Redwood needs to validate for the pilot:
1) Confirm concurrency target (sustained vs. burst). For Hosted, we have soft defaults but can request increases or propose a Dedicated pool for sustained levels.
2) Streaming requirements (chunk size, acceptable p95 for first-byte, session timeouts).
3) Token throughput expectations at peak (helps size Dedicated or quota increase).

Attachments: I attached a short form to capture the traffic matrix and the template 'performance_requirements.pdf' to confirm details — please fill or send back the traffic matrix you use for sizing (sample: connections per second by region, median/95th token sizes).

Proposed next steps:
- Alan: can you confirm whether 600-800 is a sustained concurrency target or a burst/peak? If sustained, we should discuss Redwood Dedicated (guaranteed concurrency).
- Acme to share the traffic matrix (CSV) so our infra team can do a sizing pass.
- I'll follow up with an initial proposal (Hosted quota increase vs Dedicated sizing + rough pricing) by EOD PT tomorrow.

Thanks again — looped in Laura (SE) and Logan (runtime) who can jump on a technical call if you'd like to go deeper on KV caching, connection pooling, or streaming optimizations.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alan Cheng <alan.cheng@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Pierce <samantha@acme.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme pilot - post-call recap and next steps (concurrency / streaming)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications and a matrix attached.

Answers to your bullets:
- Concurrency: the 600-800 number is our current estimate for peak sustained concurrency during regional peaks (US West). It's expected to last 30-45 minutes during traffic spikes, not 24/7. For the pilot, we'd like to validate at 800 sustained concurrent requests for 1 hour windows.
- Streaming: yes, streaming token-by-token is required for the assistant UI. First-byte p95 target is 150ms for responses <= 512 tokens. For longer responses we'd accept slightly higher p95 (<= 350ms).
- Token throughput: at 800 concurrent with 250 tokens avg and ~3 requests/sec per user during peak, we estimate ~36k tokens/sec at peak.
- Connection pooling: we use HTTP/2 with persistent connections and a pool of ~200 client connections per region. We will reuse connections across requests; TLS handshake is an expensive path, so keep-alive is critical.

I've attached our traffic breakdown: acme_traffic_matrix.csv. Also copied in Samantha who handles infra and will coordinate a technical deep-dive.

Let me know what Hosted limits look like and whether a Dedicated pilot is recommended.

Best,
Alan Cheng
Senior Product Manager, Acme IoT
alan.cheng@acme.io

--

Attachment: acme_traffic_matrix.csv (CSV, 14KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cheng <alan.cheng@acme.io>, Samantha Pierce <samantha@acme.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme pilot - post-call recap and next steps (concurrency / streaming)

Alan — thanks for the matrix and the clarity, this is extremely helpful. Quick read + what we can offer for the pilot: 

1) Hosted soft defaults (typical out-of-the-box):
   - Concurrent in-flight requests (soft): 50
   - Requests: 1,200 requests/minute per API key (burstable)
   - Token throughput: 1M tokens/minute aggregate (soft limit across the account)
   - Streaming: supported; ephemeral KV caching enabled for faster repeat prefixes

2) Options for Acme pilot (given your targets - 800 sustained for 1hr bursts, ~36k tokens/sec peak):
   - Short path: temporary Hosted quota increase for the pilot (we can lift concurrent in-flight soft limit to ~800 for a limited pilot window and raise token throughput). This is faster to stand up but is best for short-duration bursts and has no guaranteed isolation.
   - Recommended for production: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) sized for 512-1024 guaranteed concurrency units depending on throughput and redundancy across zones. Dedicated gives you predictable SLOs, consistent p95 latency, and isolation from noisy neighbors.

3) Tradeoffs & notes:
   - Hosted quota increase: lower time-to-demo; Redwood may throttle on account if sustained beyond the elevated window.
   - Dedicated: requires an MSA/SOW and ~2-3 week provisioning lead time for reserved GPUs; pricing and sizing depend on token mix and streaming overhead.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll put together a short pilot proposal and a rough Dedicated sizing (ballpark) and attach Redwood's current rate card (redwood_rate_card_v2.pdf).
- Let's schedule a technical deep-dive with Logan and Laura to validate streaming throughput, connection pooling, and failover policies. Can you do Wed or Thu this week?

If you prefer, for immediate validation we can provision a Hosted elevated window for a smoke test next week while we size Dedicated in parallel.

Thanks — will follow up with the proposal and the next-call invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme pilot - concurrency & rate limits follow-up (internal notes + action items)

Marissa / Logan — quick internal note before the tech call:

Key sizing checkpoints based on Acme's numbers (800 sustained for ~1hr bursts, ~36k tokens/sec):
- Streaming overhead: plan for ~1.2x token processing overhead due to chunking/flushes; i.e., account for an effective 43k token/sec when sizing.
- KV/prefix cache: confirm expected cache hit rate (will reduce per-token compute significantly).
- Connection pooling: Acme's plan for ~200 client connections per region is fine; we recommend HTTP/2 with TLS keep-alive and a client-side retry policy (exponential backoff) for transient 429s.

Action items:
- Logan: can you draft a Dedicated sizing sketch (GPU count, expected concurrency per GPU, recommended redundancy) so we can include it in Marissa's pilot proposal?
- Marissa: include Hosted elevated-window option in the proposal as a fast way to validate.
- I'll prepare an internal runbook checklist for the pilot (monitoring + rollback criteria + surge protection thresholds).

I'll join the technical call; proposed times from Acme (Wed/Thu) work for me.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
